title: The Dark Origins of Fairy Tales
summary: Hosts Josh and Chuck open with banter about TV binge-watching and bailing on shows, then discuss the darker origins of fairy tales compared with their Disney versions. They cover Pinocchio (Stromboli threat, cricket killing, hanging), The Little Mermaid (Andersen's tongue-for-potion bargain and ending), Cinderella (Perrault and Grimm stepsister mutilation and pigeons plucking eyes), Little Red Riding Hood (Perrault's moral about predatory wolves, Grimm's rock-filled wolf), Hansel and Gretel (stepmother abandonment, witch burned in oven), Rumpelstiltskin (name guessing, the imp tearing himself apart), Snow White (Grimm's iron shoes and heart/liver cannibalism), Rapunzel (Tangled vs. original, blinding of the prince), and Sleeping Beauty (rape in the 14th-century Perceforest version, Basile's Sun, Moon and Talia). Closes with a listener mail from Maria about signing up for college after the sign language episode, with a note on sign language sentence structure. Part one of a two-part series; part two will cover the Brothers Grimm, Hans Christian Andersen and Charles Perrault.
topics: Disney versions vs original fairy tales
fairy tale violence and sexual content

entities.name: The Sun, the Moon and Talia

segments.title: Opening banter on TV viewing habits
segments.summary: Josh and Chuck chat about binge-watching, bailing on TV shows and books that get bad, and Chuck's mortality-driven reluctance to finish things. They tease the topic of fairy tales.

segments.title: Fairy tales' dark roots and oral tradition
segments.summary: The hosts introduce the episode as part one of a two-parter on fairy tales. They explain that folk tales were passed orally among adults, and that the Brothers Grimm first meant them for adults before sanitizing them for children. Walt Disney is described as further sanitizing them.
topics: Disney versions vs original fairy tales

segments.title: Pinocchio
segments.summary: The hosts describe Carlo Collodi's original Pinocchio, including Stromboli's threat to burn Pinocchio, the cricket being killed with a hammer, and Pinocchio being hanged by the fox and cat.
topics: Disney versions vs original fairy tales

segments.title: The Little Mermaid
segments.summary: The hosts compare Disney's Ariel with Hans Christian Andersen's 1837 Little Mermaid, in which the sea witch takes the mermaid's tongue for a potion, and the mermaid ends up as sea foam after refusing to kill the prince.
topics: Disney versions vs original fairy tales

segments.title: Cinderella and its stepsister mutilation
segments.summary: The hosts discuss the original Cinderella story, the fairy godmother and midnight deadline, and the Perrault and Grimm versions in which stepsisters cut off toes or heels to fit the glass slipper and pigeons pluck out their eyes.
topics: Disney versions vs original fairy tales

segments.title: Transition to a break
segments.summary: The hosts reflect briefly on how alien observers might view these stories and then announce a break.

segments.title: Little Red Riding Hood
segments.summary: The hosts recount the Perrault and Grimm versions of Little Red Riding Hood, including the wolf eating the grandmother, the Grimm woodsman and rock-filled wolf, and Perrault's moral warning about predatory wolves.

segments.title: Hansel and Gretel
segments.summary: The hosts describe the stepmother abandoning the children in the woods, the gingerbread house, and Gretel pushing the witch into her oven.

segments.title: Break and transition to Rumpelstiltskin
segments.summary: The hosts take a break and return with the next story.

segments.title: Rumpelstiltskin
segments.summary: The hosts summarize the miller's daughter spinning straw into gold, the imp's bargain for her firstborn, her guessing his name, and his tearing his body in two. They mention the 1980s TV version and a modern show with Robert Carlyle.

segments.title: Snow White
segments.summary: The hosts discuss Disney's Snow White as the first full-length animated feature, and the Grimm version in which the stepmother wants Snow White's liver and lungs and forces her to dance in iron shoes on hot coals.

segments.title: Rapunzel and Tangled
segments.summary: The hosts describe the sexual content of the original Rapunzel, the prince blinded by thorns, and Rapunzel's tears healing him, contrasted with Disney's Tangled.
topics: Disney versions vs original fairy tales

segments.title: Sleeping Beauty and its rape-based origins
segments.summary: The hosts describe the Disney Sleeping Beauty, then the 14th-century French Perceforest version in which a prince rapes the sleeping woman, and Basile's 1634 Sun, Moon and Talia, in which the king rapes her and the queen tries to have her children cooked.
topics: The Sun, the Moon and Talia

segments.title: Closing remarks on the episode and part two
segments.summary: The hosts note that part two will explain the weirdness behind the stories and point listeners to a How Stuff Works article on darker fairy tales.

segments.title: Listener mail: Maria and going back to college
segments.summary: Listener Maria from Lakewood, Ohio says the sign language episode inspired her to return to college. Josh and Chuck discuss sign language sentence structures and the purpose of the second eye sign for clarifying who performs a verb. They give contact information.

segments.title: Sign-off
segments.summary: Josh and Chuck give contact information for Twitter, Facebook, email, and the website, and sign off.
